categories.main_business_segments: Domino’s operates three primary business segments: U.S. stores (including both franchised and company-owned locations), international franchise (franchised stores in over 90 international markets), and supply chain (manufacturing and distribution of food and other products to stores, primarily in the U.S. and Canada). As of December 29, 2024, the company had 7,014 U.S. stores, 14,352 international stores, and extensive supply chain operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Domino’s leverages proprietary technology platforms such as Domino’s PULSE point-of-sale system and the Domino’s Operating System (DOM OS) to optimize store operations and digital ordering. The company operates regional dough manufacturing and supply chain centers that produce fresh dough and distribute food and supplies, ensuring quality and consistency. Over 85% of U.S. sales are generated through digital channels, reflecting a strong emphasis on e-commerce and technology-driven customer engagement.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Domino’s serves a broad base of retail consumers seeking pizza and complementary menu items, with a focus on both delivery and carryout service models. Its primary customers are individuals and families in the quick service restaurant (QSR) segment, with franchisees as key business partners. The company is not dependent on any single customer or small group, and no customer accounted for more than 10% of consolidated revenues in 2024.
categories.geographic_coverage: Domino’s operates in over 90 markets worldwide, with significant presence in the U.S. (7,014 stores) and key international markets such as India, the United Kingdom, China, Mexico, Japan, Australia, Turkey, Canada, South Korea, and France. Approximately 65% of international stores are concentrated in its ten largest markets, and the company continues to expand globally through master franchise agreements.
categories.supply_chain_position: Domino’s occupies a vertically integrated position in the supply chain, operating both upstream (dough manufacturing and food processing) and midstream (distribution to stores), while also serving as a franchisor (brand and system owner) and retailer (company-owned stores). The supply chain segment is a major revenue driver, supplying food and products to nearly all U.S. and Canadian stores.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s 'Hungry for MORE' strategy emphasizes growth in sales, store count, and profits, underpinned by operational excellence, product innovation, renowned value, and technological leadership. Domino’s invests in digital platforms, loyalty programs, and supply chain productivity, and is committed to sustainability initiatives such as reducing carbon emissions and expanding electric vehicle fleets. R&D efforts focus on menu innovation and enhancing digital and operational capabilities.
categories.revenue_model: Domino’s generates revenue primarily through royalties and fees from franchisees (based on a percentage of retail sales), sales of food and supplies via its supply chain operations, and direct sales from company-owned stores. Additional revenue streams include technology fees and advertising contributions from franchisees. The business model is asset-light, with approximately 99% of stores franchised.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Domino’s is the global leader in pizza delivery and the U.S. market share leader in both delivery and carryout QSR pizza segments. Key competitors include Pizza Hut, Papa John’s, Little Caesars, and numerous regional and local pizzerias, as well as food delivery aggregators. Internationally, competition is more fragmented, with only a few global players. Domino’s differentiates itself through scale, technology, and operational efficiency.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2024, Domino’s reported $4.7 billion in consolidated revenues, with global retail sales (including franchisee sales) of $19.1 billion. The company achieved 5.9% global retail sales growth (excluding currency impact), 3.2% U.S. same store sales growth, and net store growth of 775 locations. Net income was $584 million, and the company maintains a substantial global footprint and strong cash flow, supporting dividends and share repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Domino’s emphasizes value, convenience, and quality, supported by a simple, efficient menu and robust digital ordering capabilities. Its vertically integrated supply chain ensures product consistency and cost efficiency, while its technology leadership (including a high percentage of digital sales and innovative ordering platforms) enhances customer experience. The franchise model offers attractive returns and entrepreneurial opportunities, and the brand is recognized for operational excellence and strong marketing.
